evidence_items.explanation: Chinchilla used more training data and fewer parameters than Gopher, improved measured performance and reduced inference computation. This challenges a simple inference from training-data scale to operating cost, but does not show that the remaining resources were small or refute Marcus's broader necessity claim.

The study reports cases where LLMs consume more energy without better classification accuracy, supporting concern about inefficiency on those tasks. Its narrow task comparison does not establish inefficiency across general-purpose capabilities or isolate internet-derived learning as the cause.

unresolved_gaps: The sources do not establish that web-scale training is necessary for the unspecified level of intelligence Marcus describes.
No cited experiment establishes that an internet-derived representation itself necessarily entails vast inference resources at comparable general-purpose performance.
Historical training-resource measurements do not provide a representative June 2026 development and operating-cost assessment.
Task-specific efficiency comparisons do not settle the characterization of the whole paradigm as wildly inefficient.
The claim leaves the capability threshold, efficiency comparator and scale of operating resources unspecified.
